channel_dna.platform_type: Open-source blogging and community platform for software developers. Welcoming, inclusive developer community. Strong SEO — articles index well in Google Search.
channel_dna.algorithm_type: Editorial curation + tag-based discovery + reactions. Articles tagged correctly surface in relevant developer feeds. Staff Picks and trending badges amplify reach. Google Search is the biggest long-term driver.
channel_dna.primary_audience: Software developers of all levels — juniors to seniors. Strong open-source, web dev, JavaScript, Python communities. More welcoming and accessible than HN. Ages 20-40 skew.
channel_dna.native_content_formats: Long-form technical articles, tutorials, project showcases, opinion pieces. Code blocks, images, embedded CodePen/Replit. Markdown-based editor.
channel_dna.platform_culture_code: Learning-focused and supportive. Unlike HN, beginners are welcome. Open source celebrated. 'Build in public' culture exists here too. Comments are constructive. Knowledge-sharing over gatekeeping.
channel_dna.account_warmup_requirements: Create profile with professional photo, bio, and linked GitHub. Write 3-5 articles before expecting significant traction. React and comment on others' posts to build community presence.

fit_scoring_matrix.best_product_types: Developer tools, APIs, open-source projects, infrastructure tools, code-related SaaS, devops tools, any product where the ICP is developers
fit_scoring_matrix.worst_product_types: Non-technical B2B products, consumer lifestyle apps, anything not relevant to a developer's professional or hobby life
fit_scoring_matrix.best_pricing_models: Open source with paid tier performs best. Free developer tier (freemium). Tutorial-led marketing works especially well — the article IS the CTA.
fit_scoring_matrix.icp_match_signals: Search your product category on Dev.to — if articles with 500+ reactions exist about your problem space, developers are engaged here.
fit_scoring_matrix.red_flags_skip_this_channel: Skip if your product has no relevance to developers. Skip if you cannot write technical content consistently.
fit_scoring_matrix.geographic_strength: Global developer community. India (massive), US, Europe, Brazil all strong.

growth_mechanics.expected_cac: $0 cash. Tutorial articles that rank in Google Search drive consistent organic traffic for years.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_traffic_spike: Published articles can appear in relevant tag feeds immediately. Google Search ranking takes 2-4 months for competitive terms.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_paying_user: 2-6 weeks for developer tools with free trial promoted in articles.
growth_mechanics.effort_level: Medium. One high-quality technical article per week can drive significant results. Quality strongly outweighs quantity.
growth_mechanics.virality_coefficient: Low on platform. High via Google Search — well-written technical tutorials rank for years and drive consistent traffic.
growth_mechanics.compounding_potential: Very High via SEO. Technical tutorials compound through Google rankings indefinitely. A top-ranked tutorial can drive 10K monthly visitors for 5+ years.

algorithm_playbook.how_reach_is_determined: Tags determine which topic feeds your article appears in. Reactions and comments in first 24 hours influence trending placement. 'Staff Picks' by editors significantly boost reach.
algorithm_playbook.what_algorithm_rewards: Well-written, genuinely educational content. Appropriate tag use (up to 4 tags, be specific). Articles that get saved (bookmark). Comment engagement. Consistent publishing from the same account.
algorithm_playbook.what_kills_reach: Promotional articles with no educational value. Wrong or too broad tag selection. Poor code formatting. Plagiarised content (community detects this quickly). Articles with no original insight.
algorithm_playbook.peak_posting_windows: Tuesday-Thursday mornings (EST). Weekday publishing gets most immediate engagement. Evergreen content performs regardless of day.
algorithm_playbook.optimal_posting_cadence: 1-2 quality articles per week. Quantity without quality gets penalised in Dev.to's curation.
algorithm_playbook.content_freshness_window: Articles active on platform for 48-72 hours after posting. Google Search lifetime is 2-5+ years for well-optimised technical content.

content_system.winning_content_types: 1. Tutorial: 'How to build X with Y' (highest search intent) 2. Comparison: 'X vs Y — which should you use in 2025?' 3. Project showcase: 'I built X in a weekend — here is how' 4. Opinion piece on a developer topic 5. Open source announcement 6. Tool review with honest pros and cons
content_system.hook_formulas: Tutorial: 'In this tutorial, you will learn to [specific outcome] in [specific time].' | Problem-solution: 'If you have ever spent hours debugging X, this article is for you.' | Project showcase: 'I built [specific thing] using only [constraint]. Here is the full breakdown.'
content_system.platform_native_tone: Educational, clear, well-structured. Code examples required for technical articles. Subheadings, bullet points, tables for scanability. Honest about limitations and alternatives. Never condescending.
content_system.cta_approach: Natural mention of your product within the tutorial context ('I built [product] to automate this — link below'). GitHub star CTA if open source. Free trial link in closing paragraph. Dev.to articles allow links — use them contextually.
content_system.content_to_avoid: Pure promotional articles. Articles without code examples in technical tutorials. Copied content. Articles targeting non-developer audiences. Clickbait titles.
content_system.cross_posting_rules: Dev.to allows canonical URL — cross-post existing blog content from your own site using canonical tag to avoid SEO duplication. Medium articles can be cross-posted. Hashnode articles can also be cross-posted.

community_outreach_playbook.where_icp_clusters: Tag-based feeds (#javascript, #python, #webdev, #devops, #opensource). Comment sections of popular articles in your category.
community_outreach_playbook.contribution_before_pitch_rule: Comment thoughtfully on 20+ developer articles before publishing your first. Dev.to community is generous with upvotes to consistent community members.
community_outreach_playbook.dm_outreach_approach: Dev.to has no direct messaging. GitHub or Twitter (linked in profiles) is the better outreach channel for developers found on Dev.to.
community_outreach_playbook.influencer_partner_strategy: Reach out to Dev.to top authors in your category for collaboration articles. Co-authored tutorials perform exceptionally well and give access to both audiences.
community_outreach_playbook.broadcast_vs_community_mode: Primarily broadcast (articles reach developer audience through tags and search). Community through comments.
community_outreach_playbook.banned_behaviours: Spam posting. Purely promotional content. Plagiarism. Creating multiple accounts.

business_stage_playbook.pre_launch_0_users: Write tutorials related to your product's problem space — without product yet. Builds SEO authority and audience before launch.
business_stage_playbook.early_traction_1_to_100: Launch announcement article: 'I built [product] to solve [problem]. Here is how it works.' Technical deep-dive on how you built it drives developer respect and adoption.
business_stage_playbook.growth_100_to_1k: SEO-optimised tutorial series targeting your ICP's most common searches. Comparison articles ('Best tools for X') where your product is featured.
business_stage_playbook.scale_1k_plus: Dev.to Listings (paid job/product listings). Partner with Dev.to for sponsored content. Contribute to their newsletter.

proof_of_play.early_stage_win: Appwrite — open-source Firebase alternative built initial developer community almost entirely through Dev.to technical articles and tutorials. Zero paid marketing. Dev.to was their primary awareness channel.
proof_of_play.growth_stage_win: Digital Ocean — their technical tutorials have been a primary developer acquisition channel for years. The tutorials are so good that developers use DigitalOcean just because the tutorials are on their platform.
proof_of_play.what_made_it_work: Both invested in genuinely excellent educational content that developers bookmarked and shared. The product was the natural infrastructure choice for developers who followed the tutorials.
proof_of_play.what_would_have_killed_it: Thinly veiled product promotion disguised as tutorials would have been called out in comments and lost all credibility with the developer community.
